exam: Friulano: its old name Tocai, why it changed (2007), what the vine is (Sauvignonasse), its Veneto name Tai.
Collio versus Friuli Colli Orientali: provinces (Gorizia and Udine), ponca, the grapes.
Ribolla Gialla, Oslavia and orange wine: the method and the hamlet.
The DOCGs: Ramandolo, Picolit, Rosazzo, Lison, all small, three of them sweet or blended whites.
Friuli Grave as the volume plain; Isonzo's gravel; Carso's Vitovska and Terrano.
Delle Venezie DOC for Pinot Grigio, and Prosecco DOC's reach into Friuli through the village of Prosecco near Trieste.
Native reds: Refosco dal Peduncolo Rosso, Schioppettino, Pignolo, Tazzelenghe.
traps: Friulano is not Furmint and has nothing to do with Tokaj; it is Sauvignonasse, the Sauvignon Vert of Chile.
Collio is in Gorizia province, the Colli Orientali in Udine; both are DOC, not DOCG. Rosazzo inside the Colli Orientali is the DOCG.
Orange wine is white grapes on their skins, not a rosé and not oxidised by definition; the colour comes from skin tannin and time.
Grave in Friuli means gravel, like Graves in Bordeaux; it is the plain, not a quality tier.
Ribolla Gialla is Rebula in Slovenia; Refosco dal Peduncolo Rosso is named for its red stem, not for a red variety of Refosco.
The village of Prosecco is in Friuli, so Prosecco DOC covers Friuli; the Prosecco DOCGs are in Veneto.
Ramandolo is the DOCG for sweet Verduzzo, not for Picolit; Picolit's DOCG carries the Colli Orientali name.
Picolit's tiny crop comes from floral abortion, not from botrytis or drying alone.

cards.f: Friulano: old name, the vine, the Veneto name
cards.b: Tocai Friulano until 2007, when the EU reserved Tokaj for Hungary; the vine is Sauvignonasse (Sauvignon Vert); Tai in Veneto (Lison DOCG).
Collio: province of Gorizia, DOC 1968, whites and Collio Bianco. Friuli Colli Orientali: province of Udine, DOC 1970, whites plus native reds and sweet wines. Both on ponca.
Friuli's flysch: alternating marl and sandstone from an Eocene sea bed, crumbly and free draining; opoka across the Slovenian border. The soil of Collio and the Colli Orientali.
Ramandolo (sweet Verduzzo, 2001); Colli Orientali del Friuli Picolit (2006); Rosazzo (Friulano-led white blend, 2011); Lison (Tai, shared with Veneto).
Oslavia, a hamlet of Collio above Gorizia; Ribolla Gialla fermented on its skins for weeks or months, often in buried Georgian amphorae, from the late 1990s.
Refosco dal Peduncolo Rosso (red stem, high acid); Schioppettino (Prepotto, peppery, also Ribolla Nera); Pignolo (Rosazzo, tannic); Tazzelenghe (tongue-cutter, acid); Terrano (Carso).
Friuli Grave (largest, gravel of the Tagliamento), Friuli Isonzo (gravel terraces, fuller whites), Aquileia, Latisana, Annia (lagoon side); Friuli DOC (2016) covers the region.
Limestone karst above Trieste, red earth, the Bora wind; Vitovska and Malvasia whites, Terrano red; the village of Prosecco lies on its edge.

questions.q: Under what name does Veneto label the grape Friuli calls Friulano?
questions.exp: Veneto adopted Tai when the EU withdrew Tocai from 2007; Lison DOCG is its showcase. Turbiana is Lugana's grape, Trebbiano di Soave is Verdicchio and Garganega is Soave's.

questions.q: In which province do the Collio hills lie?
questions.exp: Collio, in full Collio Goriziano, is the hill country of Gorizia province on the Slovenian border. The Colli Orientali are in Udine, Grave largely in Pordenone, Carso in Trieste.

questions.q: Which Friulian DOCG is a sweet wine from Verduzzo?
questions.exp: Ramandolo, DOCG since 2001, is late-picked and partly dried Verduzzo from the foothills near Nimis. Rosazzo is a dry white blend, Lison is Tai, Picolit's DOCG is its own grape.

questions.q: What is the local name of the marl and sandstone soil of Collio and the Colli Orientali?
questions.exp: Ponca is the Friulian word for the Eocene flysch of alternating marl and sandstone that crumbles under the hill vineyards; Slovenian growers in Brda call it opoka.

questions.q: Name the Collio hamlet above Gorizia where skin-fermented Ribolla Gialla became orange wine.
questions.exp: Oslavia's growers took Ribolla Gialla back to long skin maceration and buried amphorae from the late 1990s, and the term orange wine was coined for the result.

questions.q: Which Friuli DOC makes the largest share of the region's wine?
questions.exp: Friuli Grave, named for its gravel like Bordeaux's Graves, makes the largest share of the region's wine. Isonzo is the gravel terrace south of Gorizia; Aquileia and Latisana lie towards the lagoons.

questions.q: Which grape is Friulano by DNA?
questions.exp: Friulano is Sauvignonasse, also called Sauvignon Vert, the vine long confused with Sauvignon Blanc in Chile; it has no relation to Hungary's Furmint.
